blocks.label: spacr.qt.shortcuts#8
blocks.source: :func:`install` creates the bindings returned by :func:`installed`. Other actions in :data:`SHORTCUTS` are bound by the main window's menus; the scroll gesture uses an event filter. Screen-owned bindings are included by :func:`mapped`, with their scope and saved overrides. Escape handling belongs to the active screen, overlay or dialog rather than a binding installed here.
blocks.context: :func:`install` creates the bindings returned by :func:`installed`. Other actions in :data:`SHORTCUTS` are bound by the main window's menus; the scroll gesture uses an event filter. Screen-owned bindings are included by :func:`mapped`, with their scope and saved overrides. Escape handling belongs to the active screen, overlay or dialog rather than a binding installed here.

blocks.label: spacr.qt.shortcuts#9
blocks.source: Declared window-wide key sequences can be rebound. The cheat sheet carries a "Change shortcuts…" button that opens a table of the window-wide actions; a key typed there replaces the default, a key already taken by another action is named as a conflict and cannot be saved, and the overrides are kept in the Preferences store under :data:`_KEYMAP_KEY` in Qt's portable spelling, so a keymap saved on one platform reads the same on the others. Keys that belong to a single screen (Annotate, Make Masks, the field browser, Gate Editor) have separate editable rows and saved overrides, applied to both existing and new screens.
blocks.context: Declared window-wide key sequences can be rebound. The cheat sheet carries a "Change shortcuts…" button that opens a table of the window-wide actions; a key typed there replaces the default, a key already taken by another action is named as a conflict and cannot be saved, and the overrides are kept in the Preferences store under :data:`_KEYMAP_KEY` in Qt's portable spelling, so a keymap saved on one platform reads the same on the others. Keys that belong to a single application view (Annotate, Make Masks, the field browser, Data-selection boundary Editor) have separate editable rows and saved overrides, applied to both existing and new application views.

Keys that belong to a single screen (Annotate, Make Masks, the field browser) have separate editable rows and saved overrides, applied to both existing and new screens.
